([[Montverde, Florida]]) | college = * [[Creighton Bluejays men's basketball|Creighton]] (2021–2023) * [[Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball|Gonzaga]] (2023–2025) | draft_year = 2025 | career_start = 2025 | years1 = {{nbay|2025|full=y}} | team1 = [[Dallas Mavericks]] | years2 = [[2025–26 NBA G League season|2025–2026]] | team2 = →[[Texas Legends]] | years3 = {{nbay|2026|start}}–present | team3 = [[Atlanta Hawks]] | highlights = * [[List of NCAA Division I men's basketball season assists leaders|NCAA assists leader]] (2025) * 2× First-team All-[[West Coast Conference|WCC]] (2024, 2025) * [[Big East Conference Men's Basketball Freshman of the Year|Big East Freshman of the Year]] (2021) | medal_templates = {{MedalSport|Men's [[basketball]]}} {{MedalCountry|{{bk|CAN}}}} {{MedalCompetition|[[FIBA Under-19 Basketball World Cup|FIBA Under-19 World Cup]]}} {{MedalBronze|[[2021 FIBA Under-19 Basketball World Cup|2021 Latvia]]|[[Canada men's national under-19 basketball team|Team]]}} {{MedalCompetition|[[FIBA Americas Under-16 Championship|FIBA Americas U16 Championship]]}} {{MedalSilver|[[2019 FIBA Under-16 Americas Championship|2019 Brazil]]|[[Canada men's national under-17 basketball team|Team]]}} }} '''Ryan Nembhard''' (born March 10, 2003), nicknamed "'''Nemby'''",{{cite web |title=Ben Rogers on X|url=https://x.com/BenRogers/status/1996415114262843793?s=20|date=December 3, 2025}}{{cite web |title=Mavs Lead on X|url=https://x.com/MavsLead/status/1995710269343855042?s=20|date=December 1, 2025}} is a Canadian professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Atlanta Hawks]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Creighton Bluejays men's basketball|Creighton Bluejays]] and [[Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball|Gonzaga Bulldogs]]. ==High school career== Nembhard attended [[Montverde Academy]], where he played alongside Division I prospects [[Precious Achiuwa]], [[Cade Cunningham]], [[Scottie Barnes]], [[Day'Ron Sharpe]], [[Moses Moody]], [[Jalen Duren]], [[Caleb Houstan]] and [[Langston Love]].{{cite news |last1=Nyatawa |first1=Jon |title=Playing at Montverde Academy has prepared Ryan Nembhard for Creighton basketball |url=https://omaha.com/sports/college/creighton/playing-at-montverde-academy-has-prepared-ryan-nembhard-for-creighton-basketball/article_af2ca388-b855-5efe-8b61-dce0eb774569.html |access-date=December 27, 2021 |work=[[Omaha World-Herald]] |date=November 11, 2020}} Following his freshman season, he opted to [[reclassification (education)|reclassify]] from the class of 2022 to the class of 2021.{{cite news |last1=Evans |first1=Corey |title=Canadian guard Ryan Nembhard reclassifies into the 2021 class |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/canadian-guard-ryan-nembhard-reclassifies-180825285.html |access-date=December 27, 2021 |work=[[Yahoo Sports]] |date=August 28, 2019}} As a senior, Nembhard helped Montverde defeat Sunrise Christian Academy 62–52 to win the 2021 GEICO High School Basketball Nationals. He finished with 12 points, 7 assists, 3 rebounds and 2 steals and won game MVP honors.{{cite web |last1=Silva |first1=Edilson |title=Ryan Nembhard And Caleb Houstan Lead Montverde To 2021 High School Championship |url=https://basketballbuzz.ca/hs/ryan-nembhard-and-caleb-houstan-lead-montverde-to-2021-high-school-championship |website=Basketball Buzz |access-date=December 27, 2021 |date=April 4, 2021}} Regarded as a four-star [[college recruiting|recruit]], Nembhard was ranked No. 68 in his class and the No. 11 point guard according to [[247Sports.com|247Sports]].{{cite web |last1=McMullen |first1=Ryan |title=2021 Guard Ryan Nembhard to Creighton |url=https://www.zagsblog.com/2020/06/06/2021-ryan-nembhard-to-creighton/ |website=ZagsBlog |access-date=December 27, 2021 |date=June 6, 2020}} In June 2020, he committed to playing college basketball for [[Creighton Bluejays men's basketball|Creighton]], choosing the Bluejays over [[Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball|Ohio State]], [[Stanford Cardinal men's basketball|Stanford]], [[Florida Gators men's basketball|Florida]] and [[Seton Hall Pirates men's basketball|Seton Hall]].{{cite news |last1=Nyatawa |first1=Jon |title=Recruiting: 2021 point guard Ryan Nembhard commits to Creighton |url=https://omaha.com/sports/college/creighton/recruiting-2021-point-guard-ryan-nembhard-commits-to-creighton/article_1b3a8da2-c435-5738-8fff-26f511f1eff3.html |access-date=December 27, 2021 |work=[[Omaha World-Herald]] |date=June 6, 2020}} ==College career== In his college debut against [[Arkansas–Pine Bluff Golden Lions men's basketball|Arkansas–Pine Bluff]], Nembhard posted 15 points and 10 assists in a 90–77 win.{{cite news |title=O'Connell carries Creighton past Arkansas-Pine Bluff 90–77 |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401371963 |access-date=December 27, 2021 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=November 9, 2021}} On November 16, 2021, he scored 22 points and had five rebounds and five assists in a 77–69 win against [[Nebraska Cornhuskers men's basketball|Nebraska]].{{cite news |last1=Nyatawa |first1=Jon |title=Creighton's Ryan Nembhard plays beyond his years, but still 'learning every single day' |url=https://omaha.com/sports/college/creighton/creightons-ryan-nembhard-plays-beyond-his-years-but-still-learning-every-single-day/article_2cebaa06-4a36-11ec-b36e-479e78e84138.html |access-date=December 27, 2021 |work=[[Omaha World-Herald]] |date=November 20, 2021}} On February 23, 2022, Nembhard suffered a wrist injury in an 81–79 win against [[St. John's Red Storm men's basketball|St. John's]] which required season-ending surgery. He averaged 11.3 points, 3.1 rebounds, 4.4 assists and 1.3 steals per game as a freshman.{{cite news |last1=Flaherty |first1=Kevin |title=Creighton guard Ryan Nembhard out for season following surgery after wrist injury |url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/court-report-uconns-comeback-win-over-villanova-was-schools-true-ceremonial-return-to-big-east/ |access-date=February 24, 2022 |work=[[CBS Sports]] |date=February 24, 2022}} Nembhard started all 27 games and was a six-time [[Big East Conference|Big East]] Freshman of the Week honoree.{{cite news |last1=Nugent |first1=Joe |title=Ryan Nembhard is done for the season with right wrist injury |url=https://www.wowt.com/2022/02/24/ryan-nembhard-is-done-season-with-right-wrist-injury/ |access-date=February 24, 2022 |work=WOWT |date=February 24, 2022}} He was named [[Big East Conference Men's Basketball Freshman of the Year|Big East Freshman of the Year]].{{cite news |last1=Cooper |first1=Keegan |title=Creighton's Ryan Nembhard named Big East freshman of the year |url=https://www.ketv.com/article/creighton-ryan-nembhard-big-east-freshman-of-the-year/39386940# |access-date=March 10, 2022 |work=KETV |date=March 9, 2022}} As a sophomore, Nembhard averaged 12.1 points, 4.8 assists and 4.0 rebounds per game, guiding Creighton to the Elite Eight of the NCAA Tournament. Following the season he entered the transfer portal and ultimately transferred to Gonzaga.{{cite news |last1=Lawson |first1=Theo |title=Coveted transfer Ryan Nembhard went back and forth, ultimately decided ‘Gonzaga was best spot for me’ |url=https://www.spokesman.com/stories/2023/apr/25/coveted-transfer-ryan-nembhard-went-back-and-forth/ |access-date=March 17, 2025 |work=[[The Spokesman-Review]] |date=April 25, 2023}} Nembhard started every game as a junior and averaged 12.6 points and 6.9 assists per game. Coming into his senior season, he was named to the Bob Cousy Award watch list.{{cite news |last1=Craven |first1=Brock |title=Gonzaga’s Ryan Nembhard named to Bob Cousy Award Watch List for nation’s top point guard |url=https://www.swxlocalsports.com/spokane/gonzaga/mens-basketball/gonzaga-s-ryan-nembhard-named-to-bob-cousy-award-watch-list-for-nation-s-top/article_cb8bc21c-9566-11ef-a201-e78afe378937.html |access-date=March 17, 2025 |work=SWX Local Sports |date=October 28, 2024}} Nembhard averaged 10.5 points, 9.8 assists (leading the NCAA) and 1.7 steals per game and led Gonzaga to its 22nd all-time [[West Coast Conference]] tournament title.{{cite news |last1=Osman |first1=Libaan |title=‘Best point guard here’: Ryan Nembhard turns heads at NBA Draft Combine |url=https://www.basketball.ca/news/best-point-guard-here-canadian-ryan-nembhard-turns-heads-at-nba-draft-combine |access-date=June 29, 2025 |work=Basketball.ca |date=May 19, 2025}} ==Professional career== ===Dallas Mavericks (2025–2026)=== After not being selected in the [[2025 NBA draft]], Nembhard signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Dallas Mavericks]].{{cite news|title=Dallas Mavericks Sign Miles Kelly and Ryan Nembhard to Two-Way Contracts|url=https://mavsfansforlife.com/2025/07/05/dallas-mavericks-sign-miles-kelly-and-ryan-nembhard-to-two-way-contracts/|access-date=July 5, 2025|work=mavsfansforlife.com|date=July 5, 2025}} On December 1, 2025, Nembhard scored a career-high of 28 points in a 131–121 win against the [[2025–26 Denver Nuggets season|Denver Nuggets]].{{Cite web |title=Ryan Nembhard erupts for 28 points, 10 assists in Mavericks win over Nuggets |url=https://www.spokesman.com/stories/2025/dec/01/ryan-nembhard-erupts-for-28-points-10-assists-in-m/ |website=The Spokesman-Review |publisher=The Spokesman-Review |date=December 1, 2025 |access-date=December 5, 2025}} Two days later, on December 3, Nembhard earned himself a [[double-double]], scoring 15 points and getting a career-high 13 assists in a 118–108 win against the [[2025–26 Miami Heat season|Miami Heat]].{{Cite web |title=Mavericks' Ryan Nembhard: Career-high 13 assists |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/mavericks-ryan-nembhard-career-high-13-assists/ |website=[[CBS Sports]] |publisher=[[CBS Sports]] |date=December 4, 2025 |access-date=December 5, 2025}} On March 1, 2026, following the waiving of guard [[Tyus Jones]], the Mavericks decided to use the extra [[cap space]] created by the move to sign Nembhard to a standard multi-year contract.{{Cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/mavs/news/mavs-sign-rookie-point-guard-ryan-nembhard-to-multi-year-contract|title=Mavs sign rookie point guard Ryan Nembhard to multi-year contract|date=March 1, 2026|publisher=nba.com|access-date=March 1, 2026}} On April 12, Nembhard put up 15 points, nine rebounds, and a career-high 23 assists in a 149–128 win over the [[2025–26 Chicago Bulls season|Chicago Bulls]]. His 23 assists set a rookie record for the most assists in a game in Mavericks franchise history, surpassing the previous record of 17 set by his former [[head coach]], [[Jason Kidd]].{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/nba/dallas-mavericks/mavericks-news-ryan-nembhard-passes-jason-kidd-all-time-franchise-rookie-record|title=Mavericks’ Ryan Nembhard passes Jason Kidd for all-time franchise rookie record|website=ClutchPoints|last=Pereira|first=Richard|date=April 12, 2026|access-date=April 12, 2026}}{{cite web|url=https://sports.inquirer.net/671272/nba-mavs-ryan-nembhards-23-assists-break-his-coachs-record/amp|title=NBA: Mavs’ Ryan Nembhard’s 23 assists break his coach’s record|website=Inquirer|date=April 12, 2026|access-date=April 12, 2026}} On June 29, 2026, the Mavericks exercised Nembhard's team option contract for the [[2026-27 NBA season]].{{cite web |title=Dallas Mavericks exercise Ryan Nembhard's contract option for 2026-27 season |url=https://www.dallasnews.com/sports/mavericks/article/mavericks-exercise-ryan-nembhard-s-option-2026-27-22325415.php |publisher=[[Dallas News]] |date=June 29, 2026 |access-date=July 1, 2026}} ===Atlanta Hawks (2026–present)=== On July 19, 2026, Nembhard was traded to the [[Atlanta Hawks]] in a three team trade.{{cite web |title=Atlanta Hawks Acquire Luguentz Dort and Ryan Nembhard |url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/news/atlanta-hawks-acquire-luguentz-dort-and-ryan-nembhard |website=NBA.com |access-date=July 19, 2026 |date=July 19, 2026}} ==National team career== Nembhard has represented [[Canada men's national under-19 basketball team|Canada]] in several international competitions. At the [[2019 FIBA Under-16 Americas Championship]] in Brazil, he averaged 14.3 points, 9 assists, and 2 steals per game. In the [[2021 FIBA Under-19 Basketball World Cup]] in Latvia, Nembhard averaged 15.1 points, 3.7 rebounds, and 6.7 assists per game, leading his team to the bronze medal. He scored 21 points in the third-place game against Serbia.{{cite web |title=Ryan Nembhard (CAN)'s profile – FIBA U19 Basketball World Cup 2021 |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/world/u19/2021/player/Ryan-Nembhard |publisher=[[FIBA]] |access-date=December 26, 2021}} ==Career statistics== {{NBA player statistics legend|leader=y}} ===NBA===
